<!-- version: 2.41.2 -->
If you track a loan you have taken on - a mortgage, a car loan, anything you are paying off - this release makes its instalments editable again. Ticking one off and then correcting the amount always failed, with a message insisting the booking had to be income. The rule came from a time when the module only handled money lent out, where a repayment coming back really is income; a loan you are paying off works the other way round, and the check had never been told. Deleting the instalment and entering it again was the only way round it. Nothing needs configuring.

Two quieter faults in the same dialog are fixed with it, and one of them may have left marks. Editing an instalment from the loan list filled the form from the instalment rather than from the booking it belongs to. On a loan running in a foreign currency that meant the amount was converted a second time when you saved - so an instalment could double - and the account the payment was charged to was silently dropped, moving that account's balance. Both happened even if all you changed was the title. If you have a foreign-currency loan and have edited its instalments this way, it is worth checking the amounts and the account against your own records; the app cannot tell a corrected figure from an original one. From now on the form loads the actual booking, and neither can happen again.

Loan repayments are also finally named in your own language. The booking a paid instalment writes carried a fixed English title, which showed up in the entry list, the CSV export, search and the API no matter what language the household was set to. New instalments now use your language. Existing entries keep the titles they have, because that field is yours to edit and overwriting it would throw away anything you had renamed.

Full release notes are available at https://github.com/ulsklyc/yuvomi/releases/tag/v2.41.2
